final_proof:
Let \(h=\dfrac12\bigl(f+g+|f-g|\bigr)\). We prove that \(h=f\vee g\) by showing that these two functions have the same value at every element of \(S\). Fix an arbitrary \(s\in S\), and put \(a=f(s)\) and \(b=g(s)\). By the definitions of pointwise addition, subtraction, absolute value, and scalar multiplication,
\[
h(s)=\frac12\bigl(a+b+|a-b|\bigr).
\]
There are two exhaustive cases. If \(a\ge b\), then \(|a-b|=a-b\), and hence
\[
h(s)=\frac12(a+b+a-b)=a=\max\{a,b\}.
\]
If \(a<b\), then \(|a-b|=b-a\), and hence
\[
h(s)=\frac12(a+b+b-a)=b=\max\{a,b\}.
\]
Thus in either case \(h(s)=\max\{f(s),g(s)\}=(f\vee g)(s)\). Since \(s\) was arbitrary, \(h\) and \(f\vee g\) agree on every element of their common domain \(S\). Therefore, by equality of functions,
\[
f\vee g=\frac12\bigl(f+g+|f-g|\bigr).
\]
